quotes.verbatim_quote:
in general the superimposed IIm7, V7, I cadences lose the V degree and stay
only with the IIm7 and the Imaj7. However, remember that we can always use the relative
chords from minor and major chords.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Central rule governing superimposition of cadences.

quotes.topic: Superimposition color options for IIm7/I cadence
quotes.verbatim_quote:
Let's look at cadence in the key of "C" (Dm7, G7, Cmaj7). Therefore we would have 4 different
"colors" to use as superimposition ideas:

• Dm7, Fmaj7 (relative of Dm7) Cmaj7 and Am7 (relative of Cmaj7).
quotes.why_load_bearing: Concrete enumeration of superimposition colors using relative chords.

quotes.topic: Dorian over IIm7, Lydian over relative IV
quotes.verbatim_quote:
we can use Dorian ideas over the IIm7 of a
cadence and use Lydian ideas over its relative chord, which will be the IV degree (in this case,
Fmaj7).
